answer: Each agent must bind its key to a hardware token whose quartz oscillator drives a monotonic counter and whose case is closed with a saffron dyed tamper-evident seal; a public bridge contract stores one active key per token serial and rejects any second key for that serial, slashing the deposit. Extra identities therefore require extra sealed tokens, not extra keys, so n identities pay n(C+Lf) and earn nLR over L epochs, profitable only while R>C/L+f. The issuer must mint tokens one per verified human; forged seals or a copied counter remain the weakness.
